title: Termination & Transition Cheats — personal deal notes
content:
Quick scratchpad for termination / transition / escrow language to flag and suggested talking points. Personal, informal — capture thoughts so I can copy into redlines and hand off to Sales/SE later.

Context and why this matters:
- Most production contracts get messy at the end of term or on termination for convenience. Customers worry about continuity (data access, model weights, configs), and we worry about abuse (customers exfiltrating infra config or unfair early termination).
- Transition assistance and escrow clauses directly affect operational burden and cost exposure after termination. Keep the ask measurable and time-boxed.
- Escrow for model weights is rare for us; more common asks are export of customer data, logs, and a basic configuration bundle.

Clauses to highlight / flag on first pass:
1) Termination for convenience (TFC):
   - Customer asks for TFC usually with 30/60 days notice. We should narrow to 60 days and require payment for unused committed capacity or a short breakage fee if dedicated capacity is involved.
   - Redline idea: "If Customer terminates for convenience, Customer remains liable for committed fees through the end of the then-current billing period or for a termination fee equal to X% of remaining committed fees."

2) Transition assistance / winddown support: what we can offer vs what is dangerous:
   - Offer: export of customer data (in ingest format), last 30 days of logs, and a configuration snapshot (model version + routing map + runtime knobs) delivered within 30–45 days.
   - Avoid: commitments to reproduce a custom runtime or provide sustained runbooks for third-party infra.
   - Time-box: 30–60 days of transition assistance, limited to N engineer days (suggest 5–10 engineer-days for standard enterprise deals).
   - Redline idea: "Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide transition assistance for up to 45 days and a maximum of 10 engineer-days; additional services billed at standard rates."

3) Escrow and model artifacts:
   - Customers sometimes request escrow of model weights or compiled runtime. Push back: production inference includes infra & optimizations we cannot escrow.
   - Compromise: escrow of non-proprietary customer-owned models or a signed, time-limited mechanism to export customer-provided artifacts only.
   - Redline idea: "Escrow obligations limited to Customer-owned or licensed artifacts; Provider will not be required to escrow Provider-owned models, optimizations, or proprietary runtime binaries."

4) Post-termination access to logs/metrics & observability data:
   - Define retention window (e.g., 30–90 days) and format.
   - Be clear about PII and anonymization obligations.
   - Redline snippet: "Provider will deliver logs and metrics in CSV/Parquet format for the prior 60 days, redacting Provider PII and aggregated internals as required to protect Provider trade secrets."

5) SLA credits and termination for repeated breaches:
   - Customer may request termination rights after X failed SLA events. Limit it to material and repeated breaches, with cure periods (30 days).
   - Keep credit remedies primary; termination only after failure to cure following multiple severity incidents.

6) Data deletion / return vs archival retention for compliance requests:
   - Clarify that we will delete live copies on deletion, but backups may take up to Y days or may be retained for legal holds.
   - Redline: "Provider will delete Customer Data from active systems within 30 days; immutable backups are excluded and will be purged in the ordinary course subject to legal hold obligations."

Negotiation scripts / quick lines to say on calls (tone: helpful, pragmatic):
- "We can absolutely help with a structured transition — our standard package includes exports and 45 days of hands-on assistance; if you need more, we can scope it and include a fixed-fee add-on so we don't end up billing unpredictably."
- "We don't escrow our inference engine or optimizations because that's part of our operational value. We can, however, provide exported customer data and a configuration snapshot so you can reinstantiate elsewhere."
- "For termination for convenience, a 60-day notice is fair; given the dedicated capacity we reserve, we ask for either continued payment for the notice period or a modest termination fee to cover re-provisioning costs."
- "If SLA performance becomes an issue, we prefer to fix it first — our contracts typically tie termination rights to uncured material breaches after an agreed cure period."

Concessions we can consider as tradeoffs (order these with approximate internal cost expectations):
- Free transition assistance days (2–3) for small customers; for enterprise, sell a PAS (post-termination assistance) block. (Low cost to us for small deals; high for embedded work.)
- Provide an anonymized metrics dump sooner as a goodwill gesture (low cost).
- Accept a limited escrow for customer-owned models/artifacts; do not accept escrow for Provider IP.

Open questions / flags to escalate to Legal or SRE:
- How many engineer-days is reasonable as standard in our template? (Legal wants a number we can be consistent on.)
- Can SRE package a "config snapshot" that is safe to hand over (no secrets/HSM params)? Need a checklist of what to include.
- For Dedicated customers, do we have a standard breakage fee schedule tied to committed GPU months?

Notes to self:
- Keep language measurable (days, engineer-days, file formats). Avoid vague phrasing like "reasonable assistance" without caps.
- If Sales asks for 30-day TFC, push to 60 days or ask for pro-rated payment for remaining committed term.
- If customer insists on model escrow, loop in Legal + Research to explain tradeoffs; propose escrow of customer-provided assets only.

Useful copy-paste snippets (editable):
- "Provider will provide transition assistance for a period of up to 45 days following termination and a maximum of ten (10) engineer-days. Additional assistance will be provided at Provider's then-current professional services rates."
- "Provider will deliver Customer Data exports in CSV or Parquet format within thirty (30) days of request, subject to redaction of Provider PII and removal of Provider-only internal artifacts."
- "Escrow obligations shall be limited to Customer-owned models and Customer-provided artifacts. Provider shall not be required to escrow Provider-owned models, optimized binaries, or internal runtime components."

Action items:
- Formalize into a redline snippet library for Sales (put under shared_drives/legal-ops/cheat-sheets).
- Ask SRE for a config snapshot checklist (secrets scrubbed) and baseline engineer-day estimate.
- Track any deal where we grant >10 engineer-days of PA to update template numbers.

End — quick, messy, personal. Will tidy and push into shared legal cheat sheet once I validate with SRE and Legal.
